name: CD4017 Decade Counter
summary: Ten outputs, one high at a time, advancing on each clock. Pair it with a 555 and you have a chaser with no code at all.
notes: The outputs are scattered across the package in no useful order: Q0 is pin 3, Q1 is pin 2, Q2 is pin 4, Q3 is pin 7, Q4 is pin 10, Q5 is pin 1, Q6 is pin 5, Q7 is pin 6, Q8 is pin 9, Q9 is pin 11. Wire from the numbers and check twice.
Exactly one output is high at a time, which is what makes it a chaser rather than a binary counter. For a binary count use the CD4024 or a 74HC393.
To count fewer than ten, wire the output after your last wanted step back to RST (pin 15). Q4 into RST gives a four-step sequence.
RST (15) and CLK INH (13) must both be grounded for normal counting. Leaving either floating is why a breadboarded 4017 sits still or counts randomly.
CO (pin 12) goes high for counts 0 to 4 and low for 5 to 9, so it is a divide-by-ten output for chaining a second chip.
It runs from 3 to 18 V, which is the real reason to reach for CMOS 4000-series over 74HC here. Output drive is weak, a few mA, so LEDs want a transistor above about 5 mA.

pins.name: Q0
pins.note: High after reset, until the first clock moves the count to Q1.

pins.name: Q9
pins.note: Wire this to RST for a nine-step sequence, or any earlier output for a shorter one.

pins.name: CO
pins.note: Feeds the clock of the next 4017 when chaining.

pins.name: CLK
pins.note: Counts on the rising edge. The clock input has a Schmitt trigger, so slow edges are fine, but switch bounce still counts as extra pulses.

pins.name: RST
pins.note: Ground it for normal counting. High forces Q0.

pins.name: VDD
pins.note: 100 nF to GND at the pin.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit

parts.why: Reset is active high. Floating, the counter restarts at random and looks like it is skipping steps.
Clock inhibit is active high too. Left floating the counter may simply never advance.

circuit.note: Debounce the clock. A bouncing button gives several pulses per press, which is why a 4017 fed straight from a button jumps three or four outputs. Slow edges are fine, since the clock input has a Schmitt trigger.
